csa-body.readScope: Fresh complete actual main explanation read; no images or linked clinical pages inspected.
csa-body.role: Space conditions differ from Earth; duration and mission environment affect bodily responses. No clinical prediction, medicine instruction or statement that orbital free fall means gravity is absent.

csa-loading.readScope: Fresh entire explanatory main body read, including ISS equipment and capsule discussion. No video/image inspected. Numeric loads, exercise duration, medical recovery assurances and future mission promises not adopted.
csa-loading.role: Reduced mechanical loading in microgravity can affect bones/muscles; resistance/harness equipment helps mitigate this. A science accommodation example, not PE instruction or a child exercise prescription.

csa-relax.readScope: Fresh complete actual main body read, including family communications, personal materials, shared leisure and music. No video/image/recording inspected. Historical bandwidth and exact work schedules not adopted as current specifications.
csa-relax.role: Social/emotional needs are supported by relationships, private communication, familiar materials and shared activities; not guaranteed elimination of isolation or a universal coping preference.

csa-benefits.readScope: Fresh complete actual introductory benefits/service summaries read. Linked detailed claims are not implied verified.
csa-benefits.role: Specific benefit categories: environmental observations, communications, research, jobs and international cooperation. Institutional benefit overview, not cost-benefit proof or an evaluated clinical outcome.

csa-radarsat.readScope: Fresh actual About mission, image acquisition and benefit explanations through infrastructure monitoring read. No imagery, raw data, videos or technical linked tables inspected; later security/launch detail not claimed reviewed.
csa-radarsat.role: Repeated observations and composite comparisons reveal environmental changes; active radar can image without sunlight. Acquisition is requested/limited, not continuous coverage of every point or proof of cause from an image alone.

nasa-seaice.readScope: Fresh complete actual indicator explanatory body, September-series definition, seasonal cycle and related-mission summaries read. No graph/map/video visually inspected or raw data downloaded. Exact current decline rate and latest-year ranking not adopted.
nasa-seaice.role: Satellite observations since1979 permit repeated comparable September sea-ice extent assessment. The displayed monthly value is a September daily-observation average; do not confuse extent with volume or one seasonal change with the multi-year trend.

esa-debris.readScope: Fresh complete actual main explanation read: debris hazard, mitigation, dark/quiet skies, reentry risk, examples and international cooperation. No imagery/videos or linked guidelines/reports inspected. Numeric rates, deadlines and policy compliance not taught as universal law.
esa-debris.role: Orbital debris can threaten missions; disposal and collision avoidance reduce risk, while sky-observation effects and ground reentry risk need consideration. One agency’s programme is not proof that the global problem is solved.

nasa-solar.readScope: Fresh complete actual introduction, namesake, life, scale, moon, formation and structure main sections read. No diagrams/images or linked planet pages inspected. Unstable moon counts and unobserved Oort Cloud details are not needed.
nasa-solar.role: Sun, eight planets and other bodies; inner rocky versus outer giant planets and moons orbiting bodies. Use only qualitative relative arrangement, not an invented scale drawing.

nasa-phases.readScope: Fresh actual Quick facts, phases overview and all eight named-phase sections read through waning crescent, with libration opening visible. Later Earthshine/daytime/overview sections and all images/video not inspected.
nasa-phases.role: Moonlight is reflected sunlight; the visible sunlit fraction changes through orbital geometry. A normal phase is not Earth’s shadow. Use a qualitative model, no current phase/observing schedule claim.

nasa-hubble.readScope: Fresh complete actual explanatory body through six Hubble-advantage sections read. No images/diagrams/video inspected. Absolute superiority over every ground telescope, exact angular resolution and wavelength inventories are not adopted.
nasa-hubble.role: An orbiting telescope avoids much atmospheric distortion/absorption and collects light/data; it does not visit the observed planet or star. Distinct observational purpose from a rover.

nasa-rover.readScope: Fresh actual mission overview, objectives and main discovery/landing-site explanations through objective/science summaries read. No raw images/video/linked research articles inspected. Current travel records, sample totals and tentative biosignature details not taught as settled discoveries.
nasa-rover.role: Perseverance studies rocks/past habitability and collects samples for potential later study; robot exploration is not a human landing or proof that life was found.

conditions-and-accommodations.sourceSummary: Space exposes people to unfamiliar pressure/temperature/radiation conditions and microgravity. A spacecraft supplies a controlled environment; reduced body loading changes bones/muscles, with specialised resistance equipment as one mitigation.
conditions-and-accommodations.attributionLimits: Prepared task only: existing later compound Mars/SETI claim contains overlapping hazard/mitigation teaching. This case does not resolve the primary claim/age-grain issue and E1.1 stays Partial.
conditions-and-accommodations.question: Original paired cards: outside a protected spacecraft there is no normal breathable Earth atmosphere; inside a designed habitat, suitable air/pressure/temperature and water/food are provided. In orbit the craft and crew are in free fall, so ordinary weight-bearing loading is reduced even though gravity remains. Explain why meeting food/water needs alone is insufficient, and why resistance/harness equipment addresses a different need from air supply. Do not diagnose a person or prescribe exercise.
conditions-and-accommodations.expectedEvidence: Connect actual environmental conditions with physiological effects and engineered responses; distinguish supplying air/pressure from replacing reduced mechanical loading. Recognise that accommodations mitigate constraints without making space identical to Earth.
conditions-and-accommodations.nearMiss: Says there is no gravity in orbit, that more food alone solves every effect, or that an air tank alone supplies pressure/temperature and all social/emotional needs.
conditions-and-accommodations.changedCase: An original mission card has adequate air/food but no suitable loading equipment or rest routine. Identify the remaining needs rather than declaring complete accommodation. No claim that a named astronaut developed a condition.

social-emotional-support.sourceSummary: ISS accounts describe family communication, familiar messages/materials, shared meals/leisure and music as ways to maintain connections and ordinary human life during isolation/confinement.
social-emotional-support.attributionLimits: Explicit original hypothetical crew, not authentic astronaut testimony or clinical advice; no Mars-specific delay is imported into an ISS communication case. E1.1 remains Partial pending compound-claim curation.
social-emotional-support.question: Original crew case: a person has air, water and food but misses family and has little private/rest time. Compare a familiar-message collection, scheduled private family communication, shared leisure and protected rest with simply supplying more food. Explain how the supports address social/emotional as well as physiological needs, and why different people may prefer different supports.
social-emotional-support.expectedEvidence: Analyse isolation/confinement and distinguish relationships, emotional comfort, privacy/rest and physiological supplies. Explain the connection rather than assume an entertainment list guarantees wellbeing.
social-emotional-support.nearMiss: Says social needs disappear in space, or that a game automatically cures every emotional difficulty.
social-emotional-support.changedCase: A changed card makes the shared activity compulsory and removes private communication time. Reassess whether the same support serves every crew member; keep the account conditional rather than diagnose anyone.

environmental-observation.sourceSummary: NASA describes seasonal sea-ice growth/melt and a decreasing long-term comparable September extent series observed from satellites since1979. CSA describes repeated radar observations/composite comparisons for climate, land and ecosystem monitoring, with limited acquisition rather than continuous imaging.
environmental-observation.attributionLimits: Original comparison text using published source explanations, not extracted graph values, a live satellite feed or invented field dataset. No claim that source imagery was inspected.
environmental-observation.question: Original three text cards: A compares winter and summer sea ice in one year; B reports NASA’s decreasing multi-year September extent series using comparable satellite observations; C offers a single cloud/ice image with no earlier comparison. Explain which supports a seasonal account, which supports assessing long-term environmental change, and why C alone cannot establish a trend or its cause. Assess what repeated space observations add over a single ground viewpoint and what complementary context/measurements remain needed.
environmental-observation.expectedEvidence: Assess the role of broad, repeated and comparable observations in detecting/understanding change, including climate-related sea ice. Distinguish observation from explanation/forecast, extent from volume and a long-term pattern from a single seasonal pair. No numeric trend is invented.
environmental-observation.nearMiss: Only names a satellite or forecasts tomorrow; calls summer melt alone proof of a long-term trend, or claims the picture directly proves the cause or sea-ice volume.
environmental-observation.changedCase: An original changed record compares winter in an early year with summer in a later year, or changes coverage/measurement method without explanation. Identify why comparability must be checked before interpreting change; radar’s ability to work without sunlight does not guarantee continuous complete coverage.

space-impact-perspectives.sourceSummary: Space services can support observations, communications, research and jobs; missions can add orbital-debris/collision risks and affect dark/quiet skies. Reentry and disposal require attention, with international participation needed.
space-impact-perspectives.attributionLimits: Explicit original analytic roles, not fabricated community/astronomer quotations or a real funding proposal. No monetary, casualty or emissions estimates invented; no reentry prediction or debris-handling activity.
space-impact-perspectives.question: Original decision scenario: a proposed observation mission promises repeated environmental data and work for a technical team, while adding spacecraft that require end-of-life disposal. Compare three declared analytic roles: an environmental scientist prioritising useful comparable data; an operator weighing cost/reliability/disposal; and an astronomer prioritising dark/quiet skies and safe shared access. Add the ground public’s concern about reentry risk. Evaluate a benefit, a potential harm, evidence quality and a mitigation, and make a qualified recommendation.
space-impact-perspectives.expectedEvidence: Evaluate social and environmental impacts with several distinct perspectives and source-supported mechanisms, distinguishing promised benefits from observed outcomes. Recognise that who benefits and who bears risk may differ, and that a technical mitigation is not proof zero residual risk remains.
space-impact-perspectives.nearMiss: Treats all space activity as automatically good/bad, merely lists mission dates, or invents a cost/benefit score and reports it as measured.
space-impact-perspectives.changedCase: A revised proposal supplies a disposal plan but no reliability evidence, or useful data can be obtained through sharing an existing mission. Revise the recommendation and identify the next evidence needed; an agency policy is not universal law or proof of implementation.

integrated-human-impact.sourceSummary: Human spaceflight raises physical and social/emotional accommodation challenges, while exploration can provide knowledge/services and creates responsibilities for the shared orbital environment.
integrated-human-impact.attributionLimits: Original evaluation task with explicitly bounded case facts; no outcome or hypothetical priority is presented as an authentic astronaut/public viewpoint.
integrated-human-impact.question: Use the full human-condition/support and impact cards above. Assess exploration for humans travelling, wider society using services and the environment affected by missions. Give a supported benefit, cost or constraint for each category, state the source/perspective and uncertainty, and explain how a mitigation changes but need not eliminate the tradeoff.
integrated-human-impact.expectedEvidence: Produce an integrated evaluation of human, societal and environmental effects directly, rather than inheriting an overall judgment from specific-code totals. A broad impact assessment does not certify the entire physiological accommodation model or the compound Mars/SETI mastery claim.
integrated-human-impact.nearMiss: Discusses only astronaut excitement or only one technology; assumes an overall positive judgment proves every underlying technology/health claim.
integrated-human-impact.changedCase: The decision changes from a human-crewed mission to a robot collecting similar observations. Reassess which human accommodation costs remain on Earth and which disappear from the craft, while environmental/data-value questions remain.

solar-structure-and-motion.sourceSummary: The Sun is the solar system’s star; eight planets orbit it, while moons orbit planets/other bodies. Inner rocky and outer giant planets differ. Reflected sunlight and changing Sun–Earth–Moon geometry explain phases.
solar-structure-and-motion.attributionLimits: Original qualitative model with explicitly supplied positions, not a source diagram or a same-scale physical model. Numerical orbit calculations, eclipse viewing and direct Sun observation are not assigned.
solar-structure-and-motion.question: Build an original qualitative model naming Sun, Earth, Moon and the eight planets; distinguish planets, moons, asteroids/comets and a dwarf planet without a memorised size scale. Model Earth rotating for day/night and orbiting through a year; model the Moon orbiting Earth while Earth orbits the Sun. Explain changing visible sunlit fraction with three supplied positions: Moon near Sun’s direction as seen from Earth, about a quarter-turn round its orbit, and opposite the Sun as seen from Earth. Distinguish an ordinary phase from an eclipse.
solar-structure-and-motion.expectedEvidence: Explain solar-system arrangement and at least two motion-related phenomena with an actual model and causal account. Sunlight/observing viewpoint changes explain phases; Earth’s rotation explains day/night. No claim that all distances/sizes can be represented by the same small classroom spacing.
solar-structure-and-motion.nearMiss: Calls the Moon a light-producing star, explains all phases as Earth’s shadow or confuses daily rotation with yearly orbit.
solar-structure-and-motion.changedCase: A changed diagram moves Earth’s viewpoint while leaving the Moon a sphere with a sunlit half. Explain why the apparent shape can change without the Moon physically changing shape; a model view is not a current-phase calendar.

exploration-technologies.sourceSummary: Hubble collects light/data from orbit above much atmospheric distortion; Perseverance studies Martian rocks/past habitability and collects samples for possible later study; Earth-observation satellites repeatedly study Earth.
exploration-technologies.attributionLimits: Original comparative fact cards; no imagery, instrumentation operation, returned-sample promise, current mission count or empirical assessment outcome asserted.
exploration-technologies.question: Original three tool cards name Hubble, Perseverance and RADARSAT. Match each with its target, what it measures/collects and a question it can address. Explain why a rover gives local surface information while an orbiting telescope observes light remotely and an Earth satellite provides broad repeat coverage. State a limitation for each; searching for signs of life is not proof life was found.
exploration-technologies.expectedEvidence: Explain technology functions rather than only recall names; connect exploration/observation method with the question and limit. Distinguish an uncrewed Mars rover from a human landing and do not treat a telescope as travelling close to a distant star.
exploration-technologies.nearMiss: Calls every satellite a Mars rover, or says Hubble sees better only because it is much closer to another galaxy.
exploration-technologies.changedCase: A changed question needs detailed rock evidence at one surface site rather than broad repeat Earth measurements. Choose the appropriate kind of tool and explain what the other tool cannot establish; no mission construction or new discovery claimed.

losslessReviewRequirements: Choose the stable-ID allocation explicitly from existing assessment meaning, source associations, dependency roles and historical evidence; do not assume one old ID can transparently mean two new claims.

Archive the exact combined original research if later refactoring it, retain provenance/source flags and migrate complete relevant activity/assessment content rather than replacing it with a short summary.

Review every old scoped source and edge against the separated claim meanings. Any downstream belief/assessment compatibility or learner-state decision is separate and requires its own evidence; none is performed here.

A possible reviewed direction is retaining the old ID/age for its assessed SETI/Fermi strand and separating the already-present space-constraint strand into an independent primary claim. This is a curation option, not approved implementation or permission to mint a subset clone beside the unchanged compound.
